argument_markdown:
## Source-backed inputs

The following inputs are used only in their dual-confirmed scopes. ATT-0065, confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109, supplies the canonical balanced filtration 0→W_4→W→W_5→0 and the degrees deg W_4=20 and deg W_5=16 without a global splitting (CLM-0065-5). ATT-0066, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116, supplies deg L=6, h^0(L)∈{3,4} under the weak CE normalization, B_4⊂{hyperelliptic non-primitive covers}, the P^{k-1}-bundle description on reduced constant-h^0 strata, the global Abel–Jacobi incidence, and the finite etale S_6-torsor and scheme-theoretic identification with Z_ev on the ordered distinct-section stack (CLM-0066-1 through CLM-0066-6). The weak CE normalization is an explicit hypothesis, following the FND-0105 scope discipline.

## Proved step 1: dimension and stabilizers of the base

Riemann–Hurwitz gives deg R=(2g-2)-4(-2)=10+8=18. Under simple branching these are eighteen distinct branch points. Let C_18 be the stack of unordered configurations of eighteen distinct points on P^1 modulo PGL_2; it is smooth of dimension 18-3=15.

The branch morphism H^{sb}→C_18 is etale: locally at a simple ramification point the cover has the tame model y^2=t, and deforming the cover is equivalent to deforming its branch parameter; the local deformations glue uniquely away from the etale locus. It is quasi-finite because a geometric fibre is described by conjugacy classes of transitive tuples of eighteen transpositions in S_4 with product one, of which there are finitely many. Hence every nonempty component of H^{sb}, and every nonempty open component B considered in the theorem, is smooth of dimension 15.

The monodromy group of a connected simply branched degree-four cover is S_4: form the graph whose four vertices are the sheets and whose edges are the local transpositions. Connectedness of the cover makes this graph connected, and the edge transpositions of a connected graph generate S_4. Thus the cover is primitive and its deck group, the centralizer of S_4 in S_4, is trivial. Any remaining automorphism of the Hurwitz object injects into the automorphism group of the eighteen-pointed target P^1, which is finite and is trivial for a generic branch configuration. This proves finite stabilizers and generic triviality, rather than promoting a coarse branch count to a stack statement without an automorphism calculation.

## Proved step 2: constant h^0 and the P^2-bundle

By CLM-0066-2 and CLM-0066-3, h^0(L)∈{3,4}, and the h^0=4 locus is contained in the hyperelliptic non-primitive locus. Step 1 proves that every connected simply branched cover here is primitive, so h^0(L)=3 throughout B. Since B is smooth and therefore reduced, CLM-0066-4 applies: pi_*L is locally free of rank 3 with base change and the Abel–Jacobi incidence I is a relative P^2-bundle over B.

## Proved step 3: reduced-support existence

Suppose p is a basepoint of |L| on a geometric fibre. Then h^0(L(-p))=h^0(L)=3. Since deg L(-p)=5 on a genus-six curve, Riemann–Roch gives chi(L(-p))=0 and therefore h^1(L(-p))=3. Serre duality and L≅omega_C(-D) give

h^1(L(-p))=h^0(omega_C⊗L^{-1}(p))=h^0(O_C(D+p))=3.

Thus O_C(D+p) is a degree-five line bundle with at least three sections, contradicting W^2_5(C)=empty. Hence |L| is basepoint-free. In characteristic zero, Bertini applied to a basepoint-free linear system on a smooth curve shows that a general member is a smooth zero-dimensional divisor, hence six distinct reduced points. Therefore I^{dist} meets every P^2-fibre in a dense nonempty open. As B is irreducible, I and I^{dist} are irreducible of dimension 15+2=17. This proves reduced-support nonemptiness on the stated open; chi(L)=1 alone is not used for that conclusion.

## Proved step 4: ordered cover and its components

By CLM-0066-6, ordering the six distinct points gives a finite etale S_6-torsor tilde I→I^{dist} on stacks, with both source and target kept in the same unreduced distinct-section scope. Every irreducible component of tilde I has dimension 17. Over a geometrically connected base, connected components correspond to monodromy orbits in a geometric S_6-fibre; right translation by S_6 acts transitively on those orbits. No coarse-moduli torsor or Tate consequence is inferred.

## Proved step 5: recovery, stabilizers, and the image dimension

For Gamma∈|L|, weak CE normalization gives

O_C(Gamma)=L=omega_C(-D), so O_C(D)=omega_C(-Gamma).

Moreover h^0(O_C(D))=h^0(omega_C⊗L^{-1})=h^1(L)=h^0(L)-chi(L)=3-1=2. Hence |D| is a complete g^1_4 and uniquely recovers gamma up to an automorphism of its target P^1. Thus a geometric fibre of psi contains at most one isomorphism class.

An automorphism of the ordered pointed curve fixes Gamma, hence preserves omega_C(-Gamma)=O_C(D). Its action on the two-dimensional H^0(O_C(D)) induces the required automorphism of the target P^1, so it lifts uniquely to the recovered cover. Conversely, every automorphism of the cover with ordered markings is an automorphism of the ordered pointed curve. Therefore Aut(C,gamma,p_1,...,p_6)≅Aut(C,p_1,...,p_6). The stabilizer injection makes psi representable by algebraic spaces; its finite geometric fibres make it quasi-finite. Consequently the closure of the image of each irreducible component has the same dimension 17. Since dim M_{6,6}=21, each such closure has codimension 4. This conclusion uses the proved reduced-support existence and pencil recovery, not the prohibited parameter count alone. It does not say that the closure is a component of the full CE-failure locus.

## Computational hypotheses and remaining gaps

No finite computation or computational hypothesis is used. The proof does not establish that the W^2_5-free open meets every balanced component, and it gives no exhaustive analysis of unbalanced or special-curve components, no number of connected components of the S_6-torsor, no full faithfulness on arbitrary T-points, and no local lci, Gysin, Hodge, Tate, or RED-0001 conclusion.

claims.justification: Riemann–Hurwitz gives eighteen simple branch points; the branch morphism is quasi-finite etale over the 15-dimensional configuration stack. Connected transposition monodromy is S_4, so the deck group is trivial, while generic branch configurations have no target automorphisms.
claims.statement: Every nonempty component B in the stated simply branched balanced W^2_5-free open is smooth of dimension 15 with finite stabilizers and trivial generic stabilizer.

claims.justification: ATT-0066/CLM-0066-2 and CLM-0066-3 give h^0(L)∈{3,4} and place h^0=4 in the hyperelliptic non-primitive locus; CLM-0070-1 gives primitivity. CLM-0066-4 and CLM-0066-5 then apply on the reduced constant-h^0 stratum.
claims.statement: Under weak CE normalization, h^0(L)=3 on B and the Abel–Jacobi incidence I is a relative P^2-bundle.

claims.justification: A basepoint p would imply h^0(O_C(D+p))=3 by Riemann–Roch and Serre duality, producing a forbidden g^2_5. Characteristic-zero Bertini then gives reduced members in every fibre.
claims.statement: If W^2_5(C)=empty, |L| is basepoint-free and contains a dense open of reduced degree-six divisors; I^{dist} is irreducible of dimension 17.

claims.justification: The torsor and ordered scheme identification are ATT-0066/CLM-0066-6, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116. Dimension is preserved by finite etale morphisms, and the component statement follows from the standard monodromy description of a finite-group torsor.
claims.statement: The ordered map tilde I→I^{dist} is a stack-level finite etale S_6-torsor; all its irreducible components have dimension 17, and S_6 acts transitively on connected components over a geometrically connected base.

claims.justification: The residual line bundle has exactly two sections, so its complete pencil is unique. Stabilizers preserve that pencil. Representability follows from injective inertia, quasi-finiteness from the one-point geometric fibres, and the dimension theorem for quasi-finite morphisms gives codimension 21-17=4.
claims.statement: The residual formula O_C(D)=omega_C(-Gamma) uniquely recovers gamma; psi is representable and quasi-finite, its geometric stabilizer map is an isomorphism, and each component-image closure has dimension 17 and codimension 4 in M_{6,6}.

claims.justification: This is exactly ATT-0066/CLM-0066-6, confirmed independently by REV-0110 and REV-0116, using the verified Fitting scope on six ordered disjoint sections; no extension to the full Hilbert incidence is made.
claims.statement: In the ordered distinct-section scope, tilde I is scheme-theoretically the balanced CE evaluation-failure locus.

summary: On every nonempty W^2_5-free component of the simply branched balanced tetragonal Hurwitz stack, the branch geometry gives base dimension 15 and generic trivial stabilizer. The residual degree-six system is a basepoint-free P^2-bundle, so its distinct-support incidence is irreducible of dimension 17. Ordering produces the verified stack-level finite etale S_6-torsor. Recovering the unique residual g^1_4 from Gamma proves representable quasi-finiteness into M_{6,6}, hence dimension-17, codimension-4 image closures. The theorem is restricted to this open and does not classify the full CE-failure locus.

theorem_scope.base: Characteristic-zero field; nonempty irreducible components of the simply branched balanced Hurwitz open with W^2_5(C)=empty.
theorem_scope.dependency_scope: ATT-0065 with REV-0108 and REV-0109 supplies the canonical balanced filtration and degrees without global splitting. ATT-0066 with REV-0110 and REV-0116 supplies the h^0 alternatives, the one-way containment of B_4 in the hyperelliptic non-primitive locus, the projective-bundle statement on reduced constant-h^0 strata, the Abel–Jacobi model, and the stack-level ordered S_6-torsor and scheme identification on Conf_6.
theorem_scope.exclusions: Balanced components not meeting the W^2_5-free open; non-simple, unbalanced, hyperelliptic, bielliptic, plane-quintic, and trigonal-adjacent loci; number of connected components of the ordered torsor; full faithfulness on arbitrary T-points; equality with or componenthood in the full CE-failure locus; closedness of the image itself; lci, Gysin, purity, Tate, and RED-0001 conclusions.
theorem_scope.hypotheses: Connected simply branched degree-four cover, balanced CE relations bundle, weak CE relative-canonical normalization, and absence of a g^2_5 on the source curve.

theorem_statement: Let k be a characteristic-zero field and let H^{sb,bal} be the Hurwitz stack of connected simply branched degree-four covers gamma:C→P^1 with C smooth of genus 6 and balanced Casnati–Ekedahl relations bundle F≅O(4)⊕O(5). Assume the weak CE relative-canonical normalization, so on geometric fibres L:=W_5⊗omega_C^{-1}≅omega_C(-D), where D is a fibre of gamma. Let U⊂H^{sb,bal} be the open where W^2_5(C)=empty, and let B be any nonempty irreducible component of U. Let I→B be the Abel–Jacobi incidence of effective degree-six divisors Gamma with O_C(Gamma)≅L, let I^{dist} be its distinct-support open, and let tilde I→I^{dist} order the six support points. Then: (1) B is smooth of pure dimension 15, has finite stabilizers, and has trivial generic stabilizer. (2) h^0(L)=3 on B, I is a relative P^2-bundle, |L| is fibrewise basepoint-free, and I^{dist} is dense and nonempty in every geometric fibre. Thus I^{dist} is irreducible of dimension 17. (3) tilde I→I^{dist} is a finite etale S_6-torsor on stacks; every irreducible component of tilde I has dimension 17, and over a geometrically connected base the S_6-action is transitive on its connected components. (4) For the classifying morphism psi:tilde I→M_{6,6}, the pencil is recovered from the marked divisor by O_C(D)=omega_C(-Gamma) and gamma=|D|. Consequently psi is representable and quasi-finite, and Aut(C,gamma,p_1,...,p_6)→Aut(C,p_1,...,p_6) is an isomorphism at every geometric point. The closure of the image of each irreducible component of tilde I therefore has dimension 17 and codimension 4 in M_{6,6}. In the ordered distinct-section scope, tilde I is scheme-theoretically the balanced CE evaluation-failure locus supplied by ATT-0066. No assertion is made that these closures are components of the full CE-failure locus.
